reasons.text: Energy charges do not match units x tariff on 100% of bills (worst bill charged 18% of expected)
Certificates claim more than the declared monthly capacity in 26% of months
51% of feedstock comes from collectors invoicing far beyond their declared capacity
66% of certificate tonnes were generated more than 45 days after the processing month
20% of purchase invoices have suspiciously round tonnages (typical plant: about 2%)
73% of certificate tonnes were sold below the cost of recycling (average 0.82x the cost floor)

inspection_checklist: Verify the electricity bills directly with the DISCOM (units, tariff, amount); the uploaded copies do not reconcile.
Check installed machinery and shift records against the declared capacity; request production registers for the flagged months.
Visit the named collectors: confirm premises, vehicles and storage; check their registration dates and sales to other buyers.
Cross-check the certificate generation dates and category mix against the plant's process route and stock registers.
Physically verify a sample of purchase invoices with the sellers (weighbridge slips, e-way bills, vehicle logs).
Ask for the plant's cost sheet; certificates priced below the cost of recycling imply the processing cost was never incurred.
